text:
sam: quick check-in — I ran the phase-window split (separate queues for ingest vs emit). Emit p99 increased ~18% on our T4 burst traces. Not huge but consistent. Anyone seen this pattern before?

perf-bot: experiment id=exp-2026-03-18-42, cohort=A (merged queues) vs B (split queues). Summary: emit_p99_A=42.3ms, emit_p99_B=49.9ms, ingest_p50_B improved by 12%. KV_hit_rate_B=0.86 (-0.03).

carol: can you paste the queue config you used? curious about token budgets and window sizes.

sam: sure — used a conservative split to start. config snippet below:

```
continuous_batcher:
  ingest_queue: { max_window_ms: 6, token_budget_target: 18, max_batch_tokens: 1024 }
  emit_queue:  { max_window_ms: 10, token_budget_target: 48, max_batch_tokens: 2048 }
  kv_priming: { warmup_ms: 8, early_probe_frac: 0.2 }
  kernel_hints: { prefer_fast_gemm: true, fallback_threshold_ms: 2 }
```

mike: looking at the perf profile — on B we see a higher rate of kernel fallback to the generic path during long sequences (emit). That causes small stalls every few steps while the runtime switches kernels. Also KV hit-rate dips on the longer emit windows; seems we are evicting primed entries because ingest queues are more aggressive at short windows.

jen: hypothesis: separate queues changed the interleaving, so KV priming currently tuned for merged flow. Two quick ideas: bump kv_priming.warmup_ms to 12 and add a tiny seed batch policy for emit (push a small 8-token batch through to keep entries hot).

sam: nice. I tried a micro-experiment: warmup_ms=12 + emit seed batch of 8 tokens every 120ms. Results (local): emit_p99 -> 46.1ms, KV_hit_rate -> 0.892. Still 9% worse than A but much better than 18%. Experiment id=exp-2026-03-18-43.

carol: posted a trace snippet of the hot path where the kernel falls back: 

```
[emit] step=512 kernel=fast_gemm attempt->fallback generic_gemm (compile 1.2ms) kv_lookup=miss
[ingest] step=64 packed->batch commit token_budget=20
```

mike: that compile/fallback path is the culprit. Kernel selection logic uses sequence_length heuristic; with split windows, emit's seq distribution moved into a borderline zone. We could nudge kernel_hints.fallback_threshold_ms down to 1ms or adjust the seq threshold mapping. Also consider a short-circuit: if kv_priming.early_probe_frac > 0.15 and kv_hit_rate_recent > 0.8 then prefer fast_gemm even if borderline.

sam: can someone craft a safe config change we can try in prod canary? small scoped, reversible.

carol: propose:
```
continuous_batcher:
  emit_queue: { max_window_ms: 10, token_budget_target: 40 }
  kv_priming: { warmup_ms: 12, early_probe_frac: 0.18 }
  kernel_hints: { fallback_threshold_ms: 1, seq_len_boundary: 384 }
```
apply to one host-pool for 30m, monitor emit_p90/p99 + KV hit.

perf-bot: scheduled canary exp-2026-03-18-44 on host-pool=west-4-small (10% traffic). Initial 10m: emit_p99=47.0ms (vs baseline 49.9), KV_hit_rate=0.895, kernel_fallback_rate down 37%.

jen: good safety check. if that holds for 30m we can roll to 50% then full. also add an eval set of prompts that previously regressed to ensure quality not affected.

sam: ok I'll watch and roll. thanks all — great sanity check. :thumbsup: will follow up with a perf writeup + graphs in #eng-runtime later.
